subject: physics

concepts.title: Magnetic Flux
concepts.definition: The total quantity of magnetic field lines passing through a specific surface area, dependent on field strength and orientation.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Flux measures the magnetic field component perpendicular to a surface.
question_patterns: calculate the magnetic flux through a loop
find the flux when a field is at an angle
what is the magnetic flux through the plane
determine the flux linkage for a given area

solution_steps.explain: Determine the area based on geometry (e.g., side squared or pi times radius squared).
Multiply magnetic field, area, and the cosine of the angle between field and area vector.

concepts.title: Faraday's Law of Induction
concepts.definition: The generation of an electromotive force in a circuit brought about by a temporal variation in the magnetic flux linked with it.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Induced voltage scales with the rate of change of magnetic flux.
question_patterns: calculate the induced emf in the coil
find the average emf when flux changes
what is the magnitude of the induced voltage
determine the emf produced by a changing magnetic field

solution_steps.explain: Subtract initial flux from final flux.
Find the rate of change by dividing flux change by time taken.
The total emf is the rate of change times the number of turns in the coil.

concepts.title: Lenz's Law
concepts.definition: A principle stating that the direction of an induced current always acts to oppose the change in magnetic flux that created it.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Lenz's law is a manifestation of the law of conservation of energy.
question_patterns: predict the direction of induced current
determine the polarity of the induced emf
how does the loop oppose the change in flux
identify the direction of current in the moving loop

solution_steps.explain: Determine if the magnetic flux through the loop is increasing or decreasing.
The induced current must create a magnetic field that counters the identified change.
Use the right-hand rule to find the current direction corresponding to the opposing magnetic field.

concepts.title: Motional EMF in a Linear Conductor
concepts.definition: The electromotive force induced across a conductor moving through a uniform magnetic field.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Voltage is generated by the Lorentz force on charges within a moving conductor.
question_patterns: calculate the motional emf across the rod
find the potential difference in a moving wire
what is the emf induced in a falling horizontal wire
determine the voltage across a conductor moving at velocity v

solution_steps.action: Compute product of B, l, and v
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the magnetic field strength, length of the conductor, and its velocity.

concepts.title: EMF in a Rotating Rod
concepts.definition: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, the potential difference developed between the both center and the end of a rod rotating in a perpendicular magnetic field.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, In brief, Rotating a conductor in a field induces emf because of the varying linear velocity along its length.
question_patterns: calculate emf between center and rim of a rotating wheel
find the induced emf in a rotating metallic rod
what is the voltage generated by a spinning spoke
determine the potential difference for a rod rotating at frequency f

solution_steps.explain: Multiply frequency by 2*pi to get radians per second.
Use the formula for a rotating conductor in a magnetic field.

concepts.title: Mutual Inductance
concepts.definition: In brief, the property where a change in current in one coil induces an electromotive force in a second nearby coil.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, In brief, Mutual inductance depends on the geometry and relative orientation of the two coils.
question_patterns: calculate the mutual inductance of two solenoids
find the induced emf in the secondary coil
what is the change in flux linkage in the second coil
determine the coefficient of mutual induction

solution_steps.explain: Divide the change in current by the time interval.
Multiply mutual inductance by the rate of change of current.

concepts.title: Self-Inductance
concepts.definition: The induction of an electromotive force in a circuit when the current through that same circuit changes.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Self-inductance acts as electrical inertia, opposing changes in current.
question_patterns: calculate the self-inductance of the circuit
find the back emf induced in the coil
what is the coefficient of self-induction
determine the inductance given emf and current change rate

solution_steps.explain: Divide the change in current by the time duration.
Divide the induced emf by the rate of current change.

concepts.title: Self-Inductance of a Long Solenoid
concepts.definition: In brief, the specific inductance value for a solenoid using its physical dimensions and turn count.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, Inductance of a solenoid scales with the number's second power of turns per unit length.
question_patterns: calculate the self-inductance of a long solenoid
find the inductance of a coil with N turns and length l
how does inductance change with an iron core
determine L for a solenoid of given dimensions

solution_steps.explain: Divide total turns by the length of the solenoid.
Use the formula involving permeability, turns density, area, and length.

concepts.title: Magnetic Energy Stored in an Inductor
concepts.definition: The energy required to establish a current in an inductor, stored in the resulting magnetic field.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Energy in an inductor is analogous to kinetic energy in mechanics.
question_patterns: calculate the energy stored in the inductor
find the magnetic potential energy
how much work is done to establish current I
determine the energy in a solenoid of inductance L

solution_steps.explain: Multiply half of the inductance by the square of the current.

concepts.title: AC Generator Peak EMF
concepts.definition: The maximum electromotive force produced by a coil rotating at a constant angular speed in a uniform magnetic field.
concepts.key_idea: In brief, In brief, Peak voltage varies with the turn count, field strength, area, and rotation speed.
question_patterns: calculate the maximum voltage generated by the AC generator
find the peak emf of a rotating coil
what is the max emf for a given frequency of rotation
determine the amplitude of the induced alternating voltage

solution_steps.explain: Convert rotation frequency to angular speed.
Multiply turns, magnetic field, area, and angular velocity.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A square loop of side {side} and resistance {resistance} is placed in a field {mag_field_init} at angle {angle}. Field decreases to zero in {time_interval}. Determine induced emf and current.

solution_template.explain: Area of square is side squared.
Initial flux is B * A * cos(theta).
EMF is change in flux over time.
Current is emf divided by resistance.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A {num_turns} turn coil of area {area} rotates at {frequency} rev/s in field {mag_field}. What is the maximum voltage?
